lesson: In merge_tags, deduplicate tags case-insensitively while preserving the original casing of the highest-precedence source; lowercasing all tags in the output was rejected.
why: Downstream systems like the Terraform provider and saved searches require exact, case-sensitive tag matching.
quote: the Terraform provider treats tag casing as significant downstream and half our saved searches match exact casing.

lesson: In merge_tags, order the output list by first occurrence while iterating sources in precedence order and preserving each source's internal order.
why: The downstream reconciler compares diffs against this output and requires a deterministic order.
quote: the reconciler diffs the output, so it has to be deterministic.

lesson: In the merge worker, log dropped duplicate tags only at debug level with a single summary line and counts per run, rejecting per-tag logging.
why: The worker processes 40,000 resources per run, and per-tag logging would breach log quotas.
quote: the worker handles 40k resources a run and we already blew the log quota once this quarter.

lesson: In merge_tags, dash-prefixed tombstones (e.g., '-name') must never appear in the output and must only suppress matching tags in lower-precedence sources; a global kill list was rejected.
why: Applying tombstones globally would permit low-precedence or legacy sources to delete tags asserted by higher-precedence sources of truth.
quote: A global kill list lets the junkiest source delete the source of truth's tags.

lesson: For the merge worker deployment, do not use a feature flag; stage the rollout to the internal organization's sync for one full cycle before rolling out everywhere.
why: Feature flags are known to become stale and rot within the merge worker codebase.
quote: No flag - flags rot in that worker.
